name: Banana
description: High-value perennial commercial fruit crop in India (Grand Naine, Robusta, Rasthali, Nendran). Extremely heavy consumer of water and potassium; vulnerable to Panama wilt (Fusarium) and Sigatoka leaf spot.
climate: Humid tropical lowland climate; requires warmth, high humidity, and protection from severe winds.

soil.drainage_requirement: Very high; water table must be deeper than 1 meter. Stagnant water causes root rot within 48 hours.
soil.organic_matter_requirement: Very high (>1.0% OC); apply 20-30 kg well-rotted FYM per pit.

planting_seasons: South India: February - April and August - October
Maharashtra / Gujarat: May - July (tissue culture Grand Naine)
seed_rate_per_ha: Sword suckers (1.5-2.0 kg) or hardened tissue culture plantlets (3000-4400 plants/ha).

growth_stages.description: Root network consolidation, rapid production of broad leaves (up to 30 leaves total before flowering).
Transition of vegetative apical meristem to floral spike, bunch emergence through pseudostem throat.
critical_activities: Propping with double bamboo poles or polypropene twine
Denavelling (removal of male flower bud after last hand)
vulnerabilities: Yellow and Black Sigatoka leaf spot
Banana bunchy top virus (BBTV transmitted by aphids)

growth_stages.description: Fingers swell, fruit angles disappear, starch accumulates in pulp.
critical_activities: Bunch sleeving with ventilated polypropylene/blue polythene sleeve
Maintain moisture stability to prevent finger splitting

nutrients.basal_application: Single super phosphate (SSP) 300g + 10 kg FYM + 25g Trichoderma per pit.
top_dressing_schedule: Weekly fertigation splits of Urea and Muriate of Potash (MOP)
High Nitrogen during first 4 months, predominantly high Potassium from month 5 to 9
micronutrient_requirements: Banana special micronutrient mixture (ICAR-NRCB) @ 5g/litre spray at 5th and 7th month

common_diseases: Panama Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense)

harvesting.duration_days: 11-13 months for tissue culture Grand Naine; 13-15 months for tall varieties
maturity_indices: Fruit angles become round, losing ribbed ridges
Fingers turn light green, floral floral remnants fall off easily
harvesting.harvesting_method: Cut peduncle with sharp knife leaving 30 cm stalk for ease of handling.
harvesting.average_yield_per_ha: 60 - 85 tonnes/ha for Grand Naine under high-density drip planting
harvesting.post_harvest_care: Wash hands in alum water, treat peduncle with 0.1% Carbendazim, pack in CFB boxes (13 kg).
